title: EXP-01: Absolute temperature baseline (v0)
question: Can we directly predict absolute subsurface temperature?
motivation: Initial attempt to map surface satellite inputs directly to absolute temperature values across depth levels without climatology baseline subtraction.
purpose: Establish baseline performance for direct absolute temperature regression.
finding: REJECTED — worse than climatology (Test RMSE: 5.08°C). High variance across deep layers.
decisionReason: Direct prediction suffered from massive bias and performed worse than standard climatology tables.

title: EXP-02: Anomaly reformulation (v1)
question: Does predicting temperature anomaly relative to climatology improve skill?
motivation: Ocean temperature exhibits strong seasonal baseline structure; predicting anomalies isolates physical dynamics from mean climatological background.
purpose: Evaluate anomaly formulation against absolute temperature baseline.
finding: KEPT — 88% improvement over v0 (Test RMSE dropped from 5.08°C to 0.605°C).
decisionReason: Massive 88% skill boost establishing baseline for subsequent iterations.

title: EXP-03: Remove auxiliary losses (Phase 6.1)
question: Do thermocline and smoothness auxiliary losses improve test set prediction?
motivation: Testing whether auxiliary gradient penalties and thermocline-specific weighting help or hinder pure MSE optimization.
purpose: Isolate the contribution of custom auxiliary loss terms vs pure MSE objective.
finding: KEPT — auxiliary losses were hurting (Test RMSE improved to 0.594°C).
decisionReason: MSE-only loss provided cleaner gradient updates and lower test error.

title: EXP-04: U-Net baseline
question: Does a 2D U-Net encoder-decoder outperform complex implicit decoders?
motivation: Comparing standard U-Net multi-scale skip-connection representations against continuous implicit feature representations.
purpose: Evaluate 2D U-Net architecture for multi-depth anomaly output representation.
finding: KEPT — simpler architecture outperformed Fourier decoder (Test RMSE: 0.531°C vs 0.594°C).
decisionReason: U-Net skip connections preserved multi-scale spatial features across depth levels.

title: EXP-05: Fourier depth decoder (negative result)
question: Can a continuous Fourier depth decoder match standard 2D convolutional heads?
motivation: Evaluating continuous spatial implicit neural representations for arbitrary vertical query depths.
purpose: Test implicit continuous depth query architecture.
decisionReason: Implicit Fourier encoding added computational complexity without matching U-Net feature fidelity.

title: EXP-06: SST only
question: What baseline skill is achieved using Sea Surface Temperature alone?
motivation: Establishing single-variable baseline for input variable importance ladder.
decisionReason: Establishes reference point for multi-modal surface channel ablation.

title: EXP-07: SST + SLA
question: How much predictive skill does Sea Level Anomaly (SLA) add to SST?
motivation: Altimetry SLA reflects vertical displacement of thermocline density interfaces through hydrostatic pressure balance.
purpose: Measure impact of altimetry SLA on thermocline prediction.
finding: KEPT — SLA adds 87.5% of total skill gain (Test RMSE dropped from 0.618°C to 0.536°C).
decisionReason: SLA accounts for 87.5% of the total improvement gained by adding all 6 other variables to SST.

title: EXP-08: All 7 variables (final)
question: What is the peak performance achieved by full multi-modal surface tensor?
motivation: Evaluating combined surface state: SST, SSS, SLA, zonal/meridional currents (u,v), and wind vectors (uwnd,vwnd).
variant: SST, SSS, SLA, u, v, uwnd, vwnd
purpose: Production model evaluation with all 7 surface variables.
finding: SELECTED — final production model achieving 0.8072°C ocean-masked (0.5246°C full-grid) test RMSE.
decisionReason: Final production OceanEmbed v2 model configuration.

title: EXP-09: Smooth thermocline-weighted MSE (Phase 8)
question: Does upweighting loss across the 50–200m thermocline boundary reduce peak vertical error?
motivation: Issue #21 diagnostic revealed the 50–200m thermocline as the primary error band (peak near 100m). Testing Gaussian depth-weighting w(d) = 1.0 + 2.0 * exp(-(d-100)^2 / (2 * 40^2)).
baseline: v2 U-Net standard MSE (0.8072°C ocean / 0.5246°C full-grid)
purpose: Evaluate physics-guided loss weighting centered at 100m depth.
finding: REJECTED FOR PRODUCTION — Improves ARGO in-situ RMSE (0.9024°C vs 0.9148°C, -2.43% thermocline error) but regresses GLORYS ocean RMSE to 0.8197°C (+1.55%).
decisionReason: GLORYS reanalysis smooths the thermocline; weighted loss matches in-situ floats better but overfits the smoothed reanalysis target. v2 U-Net retained as production standard.

title: EXP-10: Vision Transformer baseline (Phase 9A ViT)
question: Can a patch-based Vision Transformer match U-Net multi-scale spatial representations?
motivation: Evaluating non-convolutional global attention paradigms. 5.89M parameters, 16x16 patch tokens, 4-layer MHSA transformer encoder with 15-channel anomaly prediction head.
purpose: Test transformer self-attention for long-range oceanic correlations.
finding: REJECTED — GLORYS ocean RMSE is 0.851°C, but in-situ ARGO degrades severely to 1.536°C (+74.3%). Patch tokenization destroys high-frequency mesoscale gradients.
decisionReason: Tokenizing surface fields into 16x16 patches discards localized ocean fronts and eddies essential for vertical hydrodynamics.

title: EXP-11: Graph Neural Network baseline (Phase 9B GNN)
question: Does modeling ocean pixels as spatial graph nodes improve irregular basin handling?
motivation: Testing geometric deep learning: valid ocean pixels as nodes connected to k=8 nearest Euclidean neighbors with a 3-layer GraphSAGE message passing network (89K params).
purpose: Evaluate discrete graph topology inductive biases for ocean temperature.
finding: REJECTED — Matches GLORYS ocean RMSE (0.806°C vs 0.807°C) with only 89K parameters, but degrades by 80.4% on ARGO float validation (1.589°C vs 0.881°C).
decisionReason: Message passing over a static discrete grid over-fits to reanalysis grid topology, failing to generalize to arbitrary in-situ float coordinates.

title: EXP-12: Supervised Autoencoder baseline (Phase 9C AE)
question: Can a 256-d latent spatial bottleneck compress ocean thermodynamic structure?
motivation: Testing continuous representation learning: 14-channel input compressed via 3-stage conv encoder into 256-d latent space via AdaptiveAvgPool2d(2,3) without skip connections (1.12M params).
finding: REJECTED FOR PRODUCTION / VALUABLE BASELINE — Reanalysis RMSE regresses to 0.962°C due to bottleneck smoothing, but ARGO in-situ error degrades by only 2.0% (0.899°C vs 0.881°C). Discovers seasonal thermodynamic manifold (PC1 explains 56.87% variance).
decisionReason: Bottleneck smoothing limits fine-scale reconstruction accuracy compared to U-Net skip connections, but provides an interpretable latent representation of basin thermodynamics.
